column3: Conjecture 16: constants Lprime and delta must depend only on L, uniformly in n and alpha; influence/junta bounds with dimension or log-density losses do not suffice. Tribes discussion explicitly blocks a direct bounded-junta reduction. Need uniform density increment, not small-cube samples.

Conjecture 7.3 needs a 3-Calabi-Yau category from universal-building singularities for every semisimple G. Source Conjecture 3.12 still asks for the underlying universal map; one SL3 example cannot provide the categorical construction or its functorial invariance.

Conjecture 4.6 asks for every hyperbolic metric and unrestricted complement region count. Polygon isoperimetry for one or two regions does not control the sum after arbitrary cutting; need a sharp perimeter inequality with Euler-characteristic constraints for all filling pairs.

Source Conjection 1.3 is explicitly addressed by Theorems 1.5 and 1.6: B(2q^b)=2 and the pq^3 formula; monotonicity by including divisors extends the latter lower bound to b>3. This is a source-internal result, not a new cyclotomic construction. Full proof dependency replay not performed.

Conjecture 1.1 needs the exact unknotting number for all odd positive parameters and all odd strand counts. Crossing changes supply an upper bound, while known signature/slice invariants and special families do not establish the uniform matching lower bound. One knot calculation is insufficient.

Conjecture 1 requires a field element a for every admissible p,r,k, with its Frobenius norm-product auxiliary polynomial equal to a Dickson polynomial. Finite-field coefficient matching must respect the entire conjugacy orbit; the listed small r cases and Magma checks do not yield a uniform construction.

Source introduction explicitly disproves Conjecture 1.1 using 2n^2/33 saturating edges, strictly below n^2/16, and states matching asymptotic optimality. Section 2 gives the n divisible by 66 construction. No novelty in reproducing or modifying that blowup; full construction audit not performed.

Conjecture 2.2 requires automorphism orders n^(2-epsilon) for infinitely many n for every epsilon. Direct products of familiar quasigroups give only linear-scale orders; source expressly says no superlinear examples are known there. Need an explicit Latin-square-compatible long permutation construction.

Primary PDF 1401.4502 returned 404. Literal quantifier requires one infinite C4-free graph with induced-prefix minimum degree n^(1/2-epsilon) eventually, not a sequence of unrelated finite polarity graphs. Cannot clear construction definitions or successor status from the corpus paragraph.

Source Conjecture 1 explicitly asks to remove diagonalizability from Theorem 4; Theorem 6 handles lp spaces only. Norm smoothness alone is not Euclidean self-adjointness. A proof must exclude Jordan blocks and nonreal spectral blocks for arbitrary smooth norms, not infer the answer from the record's misleading resolved gloss.

Conjecture 15 has no logarithmic loss and covers all forbidden families, including bipartite ones. Random coloring/local-lemma arguments retain dependence on Delta or a log loss; Proposition 1 already handles the non-bipartite case. Need a uniform minimum-degree-preserving sparsification, not an average-edge extremal estimate.

Conjecture 2 requires both finiteness above exponent 2/3+epsilon and infinitude above 2/3-epsilon for primitive triples. ABC only supplies a weaker implication in the source; smooth-number heuristics and finitely many ABC triples cannot resolve either full quantifier. Park Diophantine asymptotics.

Source Lemma 3.5 proves the literal midpoint lower bound for every n and x using a Legendre-polynomial reduction and recurrence. Nikolov 1402.6539 additionally proves convexity (Corollary 4) and credits Neuschel's weaker result. Exact rational grid checks are corroboration only, not a new proof.

Conjecture 3.5 quantifies over all polynomial-time algorithms and all sizes in the planted submatrix model. Convex-program lower bounds do not establish computational hardness of every algorithm. Need a genuine complexity reduction or a full parameter-regime algorithm; degenerate model/endpoint fixes do not earn credit.

Conjecture 3.4.1 leaves condition C unspecified and asks what it should be, at least unmixedness. Thus literal module hypotheses do not define a single closed theorem. Testing rings under a chosen C would change scope; no result proposed. Amenable-sequence partial results cannot supply the missing condition.

Conjecture 1 asks the magic number for every strong n-cyclotomic Delone set, with m4=7 exception. Need exclude U-polygons in every larger allowed direction set uniformly in n. Checking small cyclotomic fields or selected directions does not control all convex subsets and all directions.

Vertex-degree threshold for every k>=3 and epsilon needs absorption/connectivity across arbitrary k-uniform hypergraphs. Codegree theorems in the survey impose different hypotheses; small k instances or asymptotic numerical thresholds are not full-scope certificates. No short all-k argument identified.

Conjecture 1.1 could in principle have a finite bistellar-move certificate connecting the two K3 triangulations. Source notes millions of minimal triangulations and no computable general move bound. Input triangulations and an actual connecting sequence have not been audited; random simplification is not a certificate and large searches are parked.

Conjecture 1 requires equitable forest partitions for every tprime above ceil((Delta+1)/2). A single equitable coloring is insufficient; source planar/girth extensions do not cover arbitrary graphs. Inductive deletion must preserve both class capacities and acyclicity; no general reducible configuration established.

Conjecture 1 needs the product-fan lower bound k*d >= m*floor((Q-1)/2) for all qj>2. Moment-curve intersections prove the single-fan case but multiple complex fans can interact; a full adversarial measure construction and region-count argument are missing. Dimension counting alone is not proof.

Conjecture 1.7 asks the exact rounded value for every ell>=3. Blocking gives the lower bound and source Theorem 1.6 leaves an additive gap; an adaptive Builder strategy must close every residue class without extra moves. Finite game trees for small ell are already known and cannot settle all ell.

Conjecture 4.1 is eventual separation by the first prime outside fixed squarefree N, for all even weights. Theorem 4.4 gives the easy lower bound; Theorem 5.3 invokes generalized Maeda separability. Computing many Hecke matrices cannot establish the eventual all-weight upper bound.

Conjecture 1 is Delta+2 for every finite simple graph. Source planar Delta+6 theorem and general constant-factor entropy-compression bounds do not close the additive-two gap. Kempe recoloring must avoid all bichromatic cycles globally; no uniform extension invariant established.

Conjecture 5.10 requires top stable cohomology to survive with some trivial coefficient module for every finite p-group. Nonvanishing with arbitrary twisted coefficients does not descend automatically through stabilization; need a coefficient-change argument controlling the stable kernel, not ordinary group cohomology alone.

Conjecture 5.1 asks an absolute additive constant above n/3, while the source constructs n/3+O(sqrt(n)). The Esperet citation proves Lovasz-Plummer exponential perfect matchings, not this saturation conjecture. Need bounded global defect near the twelve pentagons, not a solved-label inference.

Retained 1405.7683v3 has a Kuriya-Shehab proof of the Lomonaco-Kauffman equivalence, not a chirality proof. No chirality passage for the literal E_(2k+1) target was found in this body; family definition and Jones-polynomial normalization remain unverified. A source-version gap is HOLD, not a refutation or known-resolution claim.

Conjecture 5.2 requires s(H)=2delta(H)-1 for every connected triangle-free H. Source regular 3-connected case uses gadgets and extra technical restrictions. Extending gadgets to arbitrary cut vertices and irregular degrees must preserve Ramsey minimality; a construction for cycles or regular graphs is insufficient.

Conjecture 1.2 asks all localized Adams d2 values, not just v3 and v4. Theorem 1.5 links the problem to alpha1-local Adams-Novikov structure; Proposition 6.4 is conditional on motivic modular forms. Need actual spectral-sequence operations for all generators, not extrapolation from tables.

Source v2 explicitly disproves the Fibonacci equality: exhaustive n=7 search finds maximum smaller than 34, rather than an example exceeding Fibonacci as the corpus prose says. The source result alone bars new credit; no replay of the enormous exhaustive search or claim of its independent verification.

Source v3 Theorem 12 exactly proves avoidance of an arbitrary forbidden matching using Delta+mu colors, and says this was a conjecture in an earlier version. Section 6 uses Berge-Fournier plus recoloring. No credit for restating that theorem; proof dependencies not fully audited.

Conjecture 1.3 requires one positive gap from both +3 and -3 uniformly over every level of Bellaterra graphs. Polynomial diameter and finite spectra do not imply expansion; source explicitly separates these properties. Need a uniform spectral or combinatorial expansion mechanism for the recursive automaton.

Source Theorem 3 explicitly implies corrected Conjecture 2 for all but finitely many 1<k<n. Removing the infinite endpoint exceptions is already part of the paper, so an anti-pencil argument is prior public work. No full dependency replay undertaken.

Conjecture 10.19 compares eternal connected domination strictly to clique cover for every non-universal connected graph. A static connected dominating set or one defended attack does not give a closed strategy under arbitrary attack sequences. Need a finite state winning invariant or a universal lower-bound adversary.

Conjecture 4.3 is a distinct-prime Goldbach statement for every even n>=12 with both primes below the largest prime below n. Exact bounded sieve checks cannot imply all even n; ordinary weak Goldbach is inadequate. A failed small endpoint would be decisive, but none was found in the executed bound.

Conjecture 2 improves m/18 to m/17 after excluding every C5^2 component at maximum degree four. Greedily deleting closed edge neighborhoods only yields weaker constants. Need a global charging or reducibility proof maintaining the component exclusion, or a graph with certified matching optimum; no such certificate obtained.

Source Theorem 2 assumes n sufficiently large relative to k. Literal conjecture covers every feasible order, every positive composition and all chosen starts. Large-n regularity cannot reduce this to a fixed finite enumeration independent of unbounded k; small path checks are not a complete bridge.

Source Conjecture 12.1 uses VDM=VDH, maxima of minimum variable-degrees at fixed deficiency, whereas corpus calls minnonmer a minimum over the class. The optimization direction must be recovered from the original version before any proof. Hitting subclass extremizers do not follow from simple clause splitting.

Source Conjecture 12.2 concerns extremal VDM>=nM-1, while the literal record describes a minimum. Source gives refined recursive upper bounds and small-deficiency data; neither an arbitrary minimally unsatisfiable example nor checking small k proves the all-k lower construction. No domain/definition repair credited.

Full-clause conjecture needs minimally unsatisfiable clause sets with at least nM(k)-1 full clauses for every deficiency k. Source full-subsumption extensions can double clause counts but shift deficiency, leaving gaps; small k and powers-of-two families do not fill every deficiency. Need uniform recurrence coverage with minimality certified.

Methuku-Palvolgyi 1408.4093 Theorem 1 gives C_P times the middle binomial coefficient for every induced-P-free family, directly implying finite limsup. The source-internal special classes are obsolete for this endpoint. Successor theorem and hypermatrix bridge read, no full dependency audit or new novelty claim.

Conjecture 1.7 requires extension of arbitrary precolored leaves for every degree d<=k, with one degree-(d+1) exception. Vizing fans may move prescribed colors; source O(sqrt(k)) bound and d<=3 cases do not preserve them at d+1 colors. Need a protected-leaf recoloring invariant for all d.

Conjecture 1.1 is eventual constancy for every real x in (0,1). Exact rational orbit samples and finitely many affine intervals cannot exhaust irrational itineraries or unbounded stopping times. Need a well-founded global invariant or a rigorously nonterminating orbit; bounded iteration would be evidence only.

Conjecture 1.2 needs alpha1+tauB<=n^2/4 for every graph. Source proves dense-cut restrictions and the induced-K4-minus-edge-free class; Mantel bounds alpha1 alone, and max-cut averaging bounds tauB alone too weakly. Need correlated extremal control, not adding independent worst-case bounds.

Conjecture 3.8 asks an extreme-point maximizer of the polynomial evaluation norm on every convex compact domain. A nonconvex polynomial can peak along a face, so moving a maximizing point to an extreme point requires a property of the integrated polynomial-space kernel. Ball/cube formulas and one-dimensional estimates do not give arbitrary-domain monotonicity.

Source Conjeture 2.3 needs multiplicity at least d+n for every antipodal n-fold open cover, n>=2. Ky Fan gives only ceil(d/2)+n; Gale proves the upper construction. Need a stronger topological intersection obstruction uniform in both parameters, not one-dimensional cover examples.

Conjecture 4.3 is a supremum over all squarefree d, with proposed extremum 17/sqrt(293). A short exact certificate for d=293 proves only the lower bound; the universal upper bound needs uniform control of small divisors of d-a^2 or quadratic-field elements. Source's extensive computations and GRH discussion do not supply that bound.

Conjecture 6.2 requires constants C,m0 for every fixed H, with critical chromatic and gcd cases separated. Bipartite tiling and small complete multipartite cases do not ensure simultaneous divisibility/absorption for arbitrary r-color classes. Need the full multipartite factor theorem; a special H would earn no full-scope credit.

Cameron-Fernandes-Leemans-Mixer 1605.09173 Theorem 1.1 proves exact highest rank floor((n-1)/2) for all n>=12. Introduction identifies it as the targeted earlier conjecture. Construction-only lower bounds are insufficient, but the successor explicitly supplies the upper bound; proof chain not fully rechecked here.

Source Conjecture 6.6 concerns all real roots beyond the penultimate peak, while source integer-root exclusion is only partial. Recurrences in the binomial basis involve signed cancellations; finite peak sets or integer evaluations cannot rule out intervening real roots for arbitrary gaps. Need a uniform sign/variation theorem or an exact isolated-root counterexample.

Conjecture 3.4 requires a proper Hamilton cycle for all n>=10 and c>=3 under the stated rainbow degree and edge count. Source tight construction at one less edge is already known. Adding one edge can alter local transition constraints; need a complete cycle-splicing argument, not recoloring or an ordinary Hamilton cycle.
